messages:
marco: Heads-up — Platform needs to finalize metric contract for GPU capacity across Hosted + Dedicated pools. Need to agree on names, cardinality, and where to pre-aggregate. Can we sync quickly?
priya: +1. Primary ask from Console is SM occupancy, per-GPU memory used, and request queue depth by pool. Also a tag for customer vs shared.
alice: Important: cardinality explosion if we tag by model + customer + gpu-type + region. We should define "owner" of high-cardinality metrics. Prefer pre-aggregated per-pool histograms rather than raw per-request labels.
jing: Proposal (rough) for metric names and types:
```
# gauge - current fraction of active SMs (0..1)
redwood_gpu_sm_occupancy{pool="hosted|dedicated", gpu_model="A100-40", region="us-east-1"} gauge
# gauge - memory bytes used on GPU
redwood_gpu_memory_used_bytes{pool="hosted|dedicated", gpu_id="g0", customer_id="cust-123"} gauge
# counter - number of queued inference requests (monotonic delta)
redwood_inference_queue_total{pool="hosted|dedicated", queue="priority|default"} counter
# histogram - per-request queue wait time (pre-aggregated minute buckets)
redwood_inference_queue_wait_seconds_bucket{le=..., pool="..."} histogram
```
carla: +1 to the names. Two clarifications: (1) For memory we should also surface per-level (model KV cache vs workspace) if runtime can provide it. (2) For Dedicated, we need tenancy labels: reserved_pool_id.
ops-sre: Cost/ingest note: customer_id label is very high-cardinality. If Console needs per-customer dashboards for Dedicated only, we should limit customer_id to Dedicated metric streams and sample/rollup for Hosted. Also set a default sample_rate for hosted detailed metrics (e.g., 1/100 requests).
marco: Good caveat. Suggest: Hosted: publish pool-level aggregates + sampled per-model traces. Dedicated: full per-GPU, per-customer metrics (since reserved capacity).
priya: UX ask for Console: we want per-route toggles (enable detailed telemetry for this route) so product teams can enable per-customer metrics. That helps control cost.
alice: Implementation debate: do we compute occupancy at runtime (fast, accurate) or in telemetry pipeline by replaying counters? Runtime can emit occupancy gauge every 10s with pool & gpu tags, that's cheapest. Avoid high-frequency traces with huge tag sets.
jing: Runtime cost: emitting occupancy per GPU every 10s across 2000 GPUs ~ 17k metrics/min which is ok. The heavy part is per-request labels. So runtime emits occupancy, memory_used_bytes, queue_depth. Telemetry pipeline computes headroom and tail percentiles from those aggregates + sampled traces.
carla: Dashboard needs: 1) pool overview (SM occupancy, mem%, queue depth, avg latency), 2) per-gpu heatmap (mem + occupancy), 3) per-dedicated-tenant view (if enabled). I'll own the Console panels but need the metric json schema for grafana.
marco: Action items:
- jing: add metric PR/proto for runtime by EOD Thu (include tag set and sample rules)
- alice: write ingest cost estimate and cardinality analysis by Fri
- carla: draft dashboard panel JSON and wireframe by next Wed
- ops-sre: propose retention & sample policy for Hosted by Fri
- priya: add route-level toggle API spec (Console + API)
Link to sketch: https://our-corp.atlassian.net/browse/PLAT-1987 :eyes:
dev-infra-bot: CI check passed for metrics schema PR #456 (jobs/metrics-lint) :white_check_mark:
ops-sre: One more: add a tag `telemetry_tier` = "detailed|standard" so downstream billing & retention can be separated without customer_id in the majority of metrics.
marco: agreed — include telemetry_tier default=standard for Hosted, detailed optional. Thanks everyone — if no objections I'll open the cross-team RFC and schedule a 30m sync tomorrow. :thumbsup:
